video_goal: Demonstrate the precise arm movements, frog kick, and timing required to swim the breaststroke.
required_subjects_and_props: Swimmer, swimsuit, swim goggles, swim cap, swimming pool

outline_steps.visual_action: Swimmer holds a tight streamline glide position, arms extended forward, legs straight together, floating horizontally beneath the pool water surface.
Swimmer's hands turn palms outward and sweep apart in a Y-shape, pushing the water backward.
Swimmer's head breaks the surface, mouth open to inhale, while hands sweep inward toward the chest in a distinct heart-shaped motion.
Swimmer's hands press together at the chest and shoot rapidly forward, piercing the water to return to full extension.
Swimmer's head submerges while knees bend, drawing heels up toward the glutes while keeping the thighs relatively in line with the torso.
Swimmer's feet flex outward, toes pointing to the sides to establish the frog kick setup.
Swimmer's legs whip outward and backward in a powerful circular motion, pushing the soles of the feet against the water.
Swimmer's legs snap straight and squeeze tightly together, toes pointing backward to finish the kick.
Swimmer holds the straight streamline position, gliding forward motionless through the water for two seconds.
Swimmer begins the next cycle, arms sweeping out and head lifting above the pool water surface to breathe.
Swimmer shoots arms forward and executes the frog kick simultaneously, returning the body to a flat horizontal line.
Swimmer completes three full breaststroke cycles, visually demonstrating the rhythmic pull, breathe, kick, and glide sequence moving across the pool.
